Hi Alex —

Appreciate the constraints. High level proposal below; I attached a compact canary matrix and an evacuation owner roster for signoff.

1) Sequencing and quiet windows
- Staged slice approach: pilot (5% of traffic) -> canary (15%) -> cohort roll (50%) -> remaining.
- Pilot + canary run in your primary VPC region only (no cross-region cut) to limit blast radius.
- Each stage has a hard 30-minute observation guard; automatic rollback if P50 latency > baseline + 30% or error rate increase > 1.5x.

2) Canary ownership and success criteria
- Owner: Redwood on-call handles rollout orchestration; Mercantile NetOps owns traffic steering and integration smoke tests.
- Success criteria: 0.5% or lower 5xx rate, p95 latency within baseline + 50ms, and a set of three smoke probes passing (auth, token refresh, inference request).
- If probes fail, RFC-triggered abort and immediate rollback target to prior pinned version.

3) Version pinning and hotpatch policy
- Pinning semantics: pin to major.minor (e.g., 1.12) is supported. Patch bump (1.12.0 -> 1.12.2) is allowed under your policy when marked as "non-functional" (security/critical fixes) and requires a single approver from Mercantile (NetOps) via the change portal. Otherwise, patch bumps follow the staged rollout above.

4) 30-minute evacuation SLA (owner map in attached CSV)
- T+0: Incident declared by any party.
- T+5: Redwood on-call triggers traffic divert to warm fallback capacity (pre-authorized).
- T+20: NetOps validates fallback health.
- T+30: If fallback unhealthy, escalate to cross-org bridge for manual slice evacuation.

Next steps: please review the attached steadypatch-canary-matrix.pdf and evac roster. If you approve the owners column, we'll add the schedule to the change request.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: steadypatch-canary-matrix.pdf (see table), evacuation-owner-roster.csv

Folks — finalizing our proposal with answers inline: 

- Pilot placement: yes, pilot will be pinned to a single subnet + AZ in the customer's VPC. We'll create an ephemeral sampling policy in the routing layer to ensure only the pilot pins hit the new image.

- RTO for fallback: warm fallback is pre-warmed to handle auth and token endpoints within the 10 minute window; we expect full traffic stabilizes in ~8 minutes based on recent drills. We will document synthetic spike tests to validate on T-2 day.

- DocuSign shortcut: Neha will publish a pre-approved emergency-patch DocuSign template that requires one Mercantile signer + Redwood engineering on-call acknowledgement. Link included in change ticket.

Rollback steps (short):
1) Abort rollout and flip traffic to fallback via routing policy (automated, ~2 minutes to start divert).
2) If automated abort fails, execute manual evacuation: cordon nodes -> scale up fallback -> explicit route shift via NetOps.
3) Post-incident: keep pinned version until root cause triage, then schedule a controlled patch with extended canary.

I've attached the canary pass/fail metrics and the owner roster for signoff. If Mercantile approves the owners and DocuSign flow by EOD Monday (May 8), we will file the change for May 18.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Lead Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
